sections.h2: Where is the Erie County recorder, and what does it handle?
sections.html:
The Erie County Recorder's Office is in the Erie County Office Building at 247 Columbus Avenue, Suite 225, Sandusky, OH 44870, phone (419) 627-7686. The counter is open Monday through Friday from 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. and closes for the usual holidays, including Juneteenth, Columbus Day and the day after Thanksgiving. When a holiday lands on a Saturday the office closes the Friday before, and a Sunday holiday means closing the Monday after.

The office records deeds, mortgages, releases and similar papers, and it also takes military discharges. It is not a place to get paperwork drafted. Its FAQ says staff are not attorneys, keep no forms, run no lien or title searches, and cannot advise on how to prepare a legal document.

sections.h2: What does recording a deed cost in Erie County?
sections.html:
The recorder's pricing page says recording costs the same in every Ohio county and is charged by page: $34 total for the first two printed pages, then $8 for each page after that. A sheet printed on both sides counts as two pages. The page's own examples put a two-page document at $34 and a three-page one at $42.

Erie County Recorder charges (source: recorder's Recording Costs page and Recorder FAQs)
ItemWhat the page says
First two printed pages$34 total
Each page after the first two$8
Marginal reference, such as an assignment or release$4 per document reference
Affidavit for transfer (successor trustee)No $4 marginal fee
Document that fails Ohio Revised Code standards$20 nonconformance fee
Copies not available free online$2 per page

Copy requests paid by card over the phone carry a processor charge, listed as a $2 minimum and up to 2 or 3 percent of the total, and American Express is not taken. The FAQ points out that every charge in the office is fixed by the Ohio Revised Code.

sections.h2: What must an Erie County deed contain to be accepted?
sections.html:
The Basic Recording Requirements page spells out what gets a document turned away. It asks for legible originals with original signatures, and it does not accept photocopies. The office checks a long list before it stamps anything.

  • A full legal description beginning "Situated in" the city or township, county and state, not the short description from the auditor's site or a tax bill.
  • A printed or typed name under every signature, and a full notary clause with the notary's stamp or printed name and the commission expiration date.
  • Both a first and last name for every party, with marital status; the page recommends the spouse of a married grantor sign and be notarized, even only to release dower.
  • A "Prepared By" line naming whoever drafted the document, and every attached exhibit that the document mentions.
  • No Social Security numbers or tax ID numbers; the office redacts the number on an original death certificate itself, and the certificate must stay unmarked.
  • For a signer acting under a power of attorney, the Erie County recording number of the power, or the power recorded just ahead of the deed in the same package.

No white-out is allowed. The $20 nonconformance fee applies when a document misses these standards, which is why the office suggests stopping in first so staff can look it over.

sections.h2: Can I mail a deed to the Erie County recorder or record it electronically?
sections.html:
Deeds that transfer property cannot be mailed. The recorder's page says any document that transfers property, or a transfer on death designation or confirmation, must be stamped by the Transfer office, and it must be carried in or recorded electronically, not sent by mail, UPS or FedEx. The office says it can e-record almost every document type, transfer deeds included, for filers with an account at one of its listed vendors: ePN-eRecording Partners Network, Simplifile or CSC.

Papers that do not need the Transfer stamp can come by mail with a self-addressed stamped envelope large enough for everything. Each document goes through recording, indexing and verification before it is mailed back, and the office describes the usual turnaround as one to two business days before it goes out in the mail.

sections.h2: What conveyance and transfer fees apply to an Erie County sale?
sections.html:
The county auditor's Property Transfers page sets the conveyance fee at $4.00 per thousand dollars of the sale price, charged on real estate and on manufactured homes. A separate transfer fee is $0.50 per line. The auditor's rate history shows $1 per $1,000 from May 1969 to March 1990, rising in steps to $4 per $1,000 since February 1994.

Exemptions need to meet a qualification on the state's DTE 100EX form, and the auditor's site has a Conveyance Fee Calculator that asks for the number of properties and the sale amount. The auditor's office is at 247 Columbus Avenue, Room 210, phone (419) 627-7746. Ask the recorder's staff where to get the Transfer stamp before you walk a deed to Suite 225.

sections.h2: How do I find a recorded deed or a mortgage release in Erie County?
sections.html:
Start with the free online search at the county's self-service site. The recorder's FAQ says indexing and images go back to 1990, with older documents being added, and a viewer can download or print images for free. Enter the last name first, then the first name, such as Smith Jane, in the Both Names box.

Two points in the FAQ help sellers. The recorder does not hold your deed: you receive the original recorded deed at purchase, and the office keeps copies only. A paid-off mortgage produces a separate release or satisfaction, so a seller who cannot find proof of a payoff should look for that recorded document.

sections.h2: What is Erie County like for a seller?
sections.html:
Erie County sits on the Lake Erie shore, and 374 of its 626 square miles are water, which leaves 252 square miles of land. According to Wikipedia that makes it the second-smallest Ohio county by land area, behind Lake County. Sandusky is the seat and largest city, Huron and Vermilion are cities, and Bellevue and Vermilion lie partly within the county. The Huron and Vermilion rivers drain it, and Sandusky is known for limestone quarries. The 1872 courthouse at 323 Columbus Avenue was refaced in Art Deco style in the 1930s.

The Census Bureau's 2025 estimate is 73,296 people, down 3.1% from 2020, and 26.8% are 65 or older. QuickFacts lists a typical owner-occupied home value of $199,700, household income at the midpoint of $71,993, and median gross rent of $933. Owners occupy 71.9% of homes and the average commute is 21.5 minutes. Sandusky City, Huron City, Vermilion, Perkins, Edison, Margaretta and Kelleys Island are among the school districts serving the county.

sections.h2: How does Erie County property tax connect to the deed?
sections.html:
The treasurer's FAQ says the county bills a year behind and that taxes follow the property, not the owner, so the balance on a parcel matters at closing. The auditor's site lists 2027 due dates of February 19 and July 16 for real estate bills, and the 2026 dates of February 18 and July 29 have passed. The treasurer's office is at 247 Columbus Avenue, Suite 115, phone (419) 627-7701.

The treasurer's page on House Bill 186 sorts the county's school districts by whether parcels may get the Inflation Cap Credit.

  • May receive it: Bellevue, Edison, Firelands, Huron, Monroeville, Vermilion and Western Reserve.
  • Will not receive it: Kelleys Island, Margaretta, Perkins and Sandusky.
  • Homestead: the auditor lists a $40,000 household income threshold for applicants who are 65 or older or disabled.
  • Overdue parcels: sold only at sheriff's sale, according to the treasurer.

faqs.q: How much does the Erie County recorder charge for a two-page deed?
faqs.a: The charge is $34 for the first two printed pages. Each further page costs $8, and a document printed on both sides of one sheet counts as two pages.

faqs.q: Can I mail an Erie County deed to the recorder?
faqs.a: No, not if it transfers property. Those documents must be stamped by the Transfer office and delivered in person or recorded electronically through a listed vendor.

faqs.q: What is the Erie County conveyance fee?
faqs.a: The auditor's page lists $4.00 per thousand dollars of the sale price, plus a $0.50 per line transfer fee. Call the auditor at (419) 627-7746 to confirm figures for your closing.

faqs.q: Does the Erie County recorder keep my original deed?
faqs.a: No. The recorder's FAQ says it keeps copies only and that you receive the original recorded deed when you buy. A mortgage payoff produces its own release document.

faqs.q: What time does the Erie County recorder open and close?
faqs.a: The office is open Monday through Friday from 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. Closed days include Veterans Day, Thanksgiving, the day after Thanksgiving and Christmas Day.
